prompt:
INPUT: the attached image is the approved character — her Fantasy card; keep her. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — the personification of Oil, of the Carbon Nation, seen in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut, skin tone and body proportions; expression and hair motion may change, and her hair may be worn differently only as SCENE's Hair line says. The substance shows ONLY as a small accessory, an object around her, or the object PROP says she holds — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume.

DESIGN (accessory hints only): her element's visual language — two faces of one element: black soot and clear diamond; hexagonal lattices (graphite, graphene) as patterns, pencil-graphite grey, carbon-fibre weave; it bonds with everything and is the frame of all life — may inform at most one small accessory, a hair ornament or an object beside her, in its palette (charcoal black, graphite grey, diamond white, a single living green). The clothes keep the chosen outfit's own colours; her skin, hair and eyes stay as in the attached image.

STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp fabric and accessory detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and natural lighting.

AGE: the same adult woman as in the attached image — keep her own face shape, cheekbones, eye proportions and skin tone exactly; minimal facial lines (no nasolabial folds, crow's feet, under-eye bags or cheek creases).

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her in the outfit chosen in SCENE; her element shows only through accessories and objects around her — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume. Everything else follows SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; COMPOSITION in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

CROP: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame. This crop wins over every other line: details apply only to the part that shows, and the outfit reads through its visible neckline, straps, fabric and colour. Never widen the framing to show a hidden support, hand or leg; a limb crossing the edge runs naturally on past it, never cut off or fading out inside the image.

SETTING: a real present-day place where Carbon (C) is actually made, worked or used — Place in SCENE names it. Its tools, materials and machines are the real ones of that trade; the element's own visual language (two faces of one element: black soot and clear diamond; hexagonal lattices (graphite, graphene) as patterns, pencil-graphite grey, carbon-fibre weave; it bonds with everything and is the frame of all life) lives in the surroundings, light and materials, never in her clothes. She is at ease there, in the outfit SCENE describes.

SCENE (chosen):
Place: a wide salt pan at low tide, shallow brine mirroring the sky, wooden rakes and heaps of white salt
Outfit: a fitted archery top with an arm guard
POSTURE: standing.
COMPOSITION: a chest-up shot of her face, shoulders and expression; body facing the camera; head tilted slightly; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand is in PROP.
PROP: with both hands she dries her hair with a towel — her own right hand presses the towel to the top of her head, her own left hand holds the towel at the side of her hair.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: lidded half-open eyes, slack mouth, brows flat and unengaged.
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — more bare shoulder and collarbone inside the crop; the crop stays exactly where CROP sets it and never moves down to show more; cover the chest

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face, hair and body — not its garment, armor, regalia, ornaments, mecha plates or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; the part of that outfit inside the crop must read at first glance in its own colours. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her element belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her element's palette, materials, patterns or regalia.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera exactly as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same. No default card pose, no default front-facing portrait.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. Where the place is busy, other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her. No logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (C) and atomic number (6) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may stay outside the crop, and fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.
